The '''2019–20 Ekstraklasa''' (also known as '''PKO Bank Polski Ekstraklasa''' due to its [[Sponsor (commercial)|sponsorship]] by [[PKO Bank Polski]])<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ekstraklasa.org/aktualnosci/pko-bank-polski-partnerem-tytularnym-ekstraklasy-13894 |title=PKO Bank Polski partnerem tytularnym Ekstraklasy |publisher=ekstraklasa.org |date=28 June 2019 |access-date=28 June 2019 |language=pl |archive-date=1 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190701062604/http://ekstraklasa.org/aktualnosci/pko-bank-polski-partnerem-tytularnym-ekstraklasy-13894 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tvp.info/43235057/pko-bp-sponsorem-tytularnym-pilkarskiej-ekstraklasy |title=PKO BP sponsorem tytularnym piłkarskiej Ekstraklasy |publisher=tvp.info |date=26 June 2019 |access-date=26 June 2019 |language=pl}}</ref> was the 94th season of [[List of Polish football champions|the Polish Football Championship]], the 86th season of [[Sports league|the highest tier domestic division]] in the [[Polish football league system]] since its establishment in [[1927 Ekstraklasa|1927]] and the 12th season of the [[Ekstraklasa]] under its current title. The league was operated by the Ekstraklasa [[S.A. (corporation)|SA]].

The regular season was played as a [[round-robin tournament]]. A total of 16 teams participated, 14 of which competed in the league during the [[2018–19 Ekstraklasa|previous season]], while the remaining two were promoted from the [[2018–19 I liga]]. It is the third Ekstraklasa season to use [[Video assistant referee|VAR]]. The season started on 19 July 2019 and concluded on 19 July 2020 (the fixtures were announced on 3 June 2019 and revised on 13 May 2020 due to the outbreak of [[COVID-19 pandemic in Poland|COVID-19 pandemic]]).<ref name="Terminarz1">{{cite web |url=https://ekstraklasa.org/aktualnosci/znamy-terminarz-nowego-sezonu-2019-20-13885 |title=Znamy terminarz nowego sezonu 2019/20 |publisher=ekstraklasa.org |date=3 June 2019 |access-date=3 June 2019 |language=pl |archive-date=6 June 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190606085456/http://ekstraklasa.org/aktualnosci/znamy-terminarz-nowego-sezonu-2019-20-13885 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="Terminarz2">{{cite web |url=http://www.90minut.pl/news/296/news2964381-Terminarz-Ekstraklasy-2019-20.html |title=Terminarz Ekstraklasy 2019/20 |publisher=90minut.pl |date=3 June 2019 |access-date=3 June 2019 |language=pl}}</ref><ref name="Terminarz3">{{cite web |url=http://www.90minut.pl/news/303/news3037525-Ramowy-terminarz-dokonczenia-sezonu-2019-2020.html |title=Ramowy terminarz dokończenia sezonu 2019/2020 |publisher=90minut.pl |date=13 May 2020 |access-date=13 May 2020 |language=pl}}</ref> After the 20th matchday the league went on a winter break between 23 December 2019 and 8 February 2020. On 13 March 2020, the Ekstraklasa SA suspended the league due to the outbreak of COVID-19 pandemic.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ekstraklasa.org/aktualnosci/matches-of-pko-bank-polski-ekstraklasa-postponed-14560 |title=Matches of PKO Bank Polski Ekstraklasa postponed |publisher=ekstraklasa.org |date=13 March 2020 |access-date=13 March 2020 |language=en |archive-date=12 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200612171053/https://ekstraklasa.org/aktualnosci/matches-of-pko-bank-polski-ekstraklasa-postponed-14560 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.90minut.pl/news/303/news3030899-Rozgrywki-PKO-Ekstraklasy-zawieszone.html |title=Rozgrywki PKO Ekstraklasy zawieszone |publisher=90minut.pl |date=13 March 2020 |access-date=13 March 2020 |language=pl}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://ekstraklasa.org/aktualnosci/mecze-ekstraklasy-odwolane-do-26-kwietnia-wlacznie-14567 |title=Mecze Ekstraklasy odwołane do 26 kwietnia włącznie |publisher=ekstraklasa.org |date=20 March 2020 |access-date=20 March 2020 |language=pl |archive-date=4 April 2020 |url=http://www.90minut.pl/news/303/news3031739-Rozgrywki-PKO-Ekstraklasy-zawieszone-do-26-kwietnia.html |title=Rozgrywki PKO Ekstraklasy zawieszone do 26 kwietnia |publisher=90minut.pl |date=20 March 2020 |access-date=20 March 2020 |language=pl}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.90minut.pl/news/303/news3035357-Mecze-PKO-Ekstraklasy-moga-sie-odbywac-od-29-maja.html |title=Mecze PKO Ekstraklasy mogą się odbywać od 29 maja |publisher=90minut.pl |date=25 April 2020 |access-date=25 April 2020 |language=pl}}</ref> After consultation with the [[Second Cabinet of Mateusz Morawiecki|Polish government]], the league resumed [[Behind closed doors (sport)|behind closed doors]] without any spectators on 29 May 2020.<ref>{{cite web |title=WSZYSCY PIŁKARZE EKSTRAKLASY ZDROWI. ZNAMY TERMINARZ PIERWSZYCH KOLEJEK |url=https://piast-gliwice.eu/aktualnosci/newsy/wszyscy-pilkarze-ekstraklasy-zdrowi-znamy-terminarz-pierwszych-kolejek |website=piast-gliwice.eu |publisher=Gliwicki Klub Sportowy Piast Gliwice |access-date=4 April 2025 |language=pl |date=8 May 2020}}</ref> All matches of 31–37 round have been played with "no more than 25 percent of the number of seats allocated to the public".<ref>{{cite web |title=Oficjalnie: Kibice mogą wrócić na stadiony! Nowe wytyczne rządu |url=https://www.sport.pl/pilka/7,65039,26027333,oficjalnie-kibice-moga-wrocic-na-stadiony-nowe-wytyczne-rzadu.html |website=sport.pl |access-date=4 April 2025 |language=pl |date=12 June 2020}}</ref>

Each team played a total of 30 matches in the regular season, half at home and half away. After the 30th round, the league split into two groups: ''championship round'' (top eight teams) and ''relegation round'' (bottom eight teams). Each team played 7 more games (teams ranked 1 to 4 and 9 to 12 played four times at home). Therefore, each team played a total of 37 matches. The team at the top of the Championship round won the league title. However, the rules for promotion and relegation from the league have changed: starting from the 2019–20 season, three teams were relegated from Ekstraklasa to [[I liga]], while from the I liga to Ekstraklasa two teams advanced directly, while teams from 3-6 places fought in a play-off where the winner was awarded with a promotion to Ekstraklasa.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://sportowefakty.wp.pl/pilka-nozna/738060/beda-zmiany-w-ekstraklasie-trzy-druzyny-spadna-z-ligi |title=Będą zmiany w Ekstraklasie. Trzy drużyny spadną z ligi |publisher=sportowyfakty.wp.pl |date=15 February 2018 |access-date=24 May 2019 |language=pl}}</ref>

The defending champions were [[Piast Gliwice]], who won their 1st Polish title [[2018–19 Ekstraklasa|the previous season]]. The two clubs promoted were [[Raków Częstochowa]], returning to Ekstraklasa after 21 years, as well as [[ŁKS Łódź]], who make a return to Ekstraklasa after 7 years. [[Legia Warsaw]] clinched their fourteenth Ekstraklasa title on the twenty eight matchday of the season, after a 2–0 win against [[KS Cracovia (football)|Cracovia]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ekstraklasa.org/aktualnosci/legia-warszawa-mistrzem-polski-2019-2020-14735 |title=Legia Warszawa mistrzem Polski 2019/2020! |publisher=Ekstraklasa |date=12 July 2020 |access-date=25 May 2021 |language=pl |archive-date=22 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210422060727/https://ekstraklasa.org/aktualnosci/legia-warszawa-mistrzem-polski-2019-2020-14735 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
